manifesto: Cherut started with a simple frustration: every tool that claimed to help you live better only made the system more complicated. Separate apps for habits, tasks, goals, finances, journaling — none of them talking to each other, none of them tied to a why.

We spent a year hopping between Notion, Todoist, spreadsheets and paper notebooks. The missing piece was never another app. It was a coherent method — one that connects what you do today to who you are becoming.

So we built Cherut. Opinionated about method. Quiet about everything else. We believe the best productivity tool is the one you actually use — one that respects your attention and earns your trust by getting out of the way.

hero.title: Set up your system in 30 minutes
hero.lead: A step-by-step guide to get ALL IN ALL THE TIME from day one.

gettingStartedPage.checklistHeading: Seven steps. Thirty minutes. One system.

steps.title: Complete your profile
steps.body: Upload a photo, set your timezone, choose notification settings and define your working hours for better task planning.

steps.title: Define your core values
steps.body: Navigate to Values and choose 3–5 principles that guide your decisions. Write a short description for each and rank them. These become your compass.

steps.title: Set up your life areas
steps.body: Create 4–6 life domains (Health, Career, Finance, Relationships…). Write a vision statement for each and set priority levels.

steps.title: Create your first OKRs
steps.body: Start with 1–2 objectives per life area. Write inspiring, qualitative objectives, then add 2–4 measurable key results with specific deadlines.

steps.title: Build success habits
steps.body: Create 3–5 keystone habits that support multiple objectives. Start small, set specific triggers, and link habits to your life areas and OKRs.

steps.title: Plan your first week
steps.body: Break key results into specific tasks. Schedule focused work blocks for the most important tasks. Plan habit execution times throughout the week.

steps.title: Set up tracking & reviews
steps.body: Configure your dashboard, schedule daily check-ins (5 min) and weekly reviews (30 min). Enable analytics to understand performance patterns.

tips.title: Start small, think big
tips.body: Consistent small wins beat ambitious failures. Build momentum early — the system compounds when you actually use it.

tips.title: Weekly reviews are non-negotiable
tips.body: Schedule 30 minutes every Sunday. Celebrate wins, analyze obstacles, adjust plans. This single habit is what separates drifters from executors.

tips.title: Connect everything to values
tips.body: When goals align with your core values, motivation becomes automatic. Always ask: why does this matter to me?

gettingStartedPage.ctaSub: The system is only as powerful as your commitment to using it.

hero.title: How can we help?

articles.title: What is Cherut?
articles.body: Cherut is a personal operating system that connects your habits, tasks, OKRs, journal and vision board in one place. Start by setting up your Life Areas and creating your first Objective.

articles.title: Setting up your account
articles.body: After signing up, you will be guided through a short onboarding flow. Pick the modules you want active — you can turn others on later from Settings.

articles.title: Choosing your first module
articles.body: Not sure where to start? Most people begin with Habits or Tasks. Once you have a rhythm, add OKRs to give your daily actions a direction.

articles.title: Creating a habit
articles.body: Go to Habits → New Habit. Set a name, frequency (daily, weekdays, or custom days), and optionally link it to a Life Area or OKR.

articles.title: How streaks work
articles.body: A streak increments each day you complete a habit. Missing a day breaks the streak, but your completion history is always preserved.

articles.title: Archiving vs deleting
articles.body: Archive a habit to pause it without losing history. Delete only when you want to remove all records permanently.

articles.title: Creating a board
articles.body: Go to Tasks and click "New Board". Give it a name and optionally assign it to a Life Area. Boards have columns you can rename and reorder.

articles.title: Moving tasks between columns
articles.body: Drag a task card to any column, or open the task and change its status from the dropdown.

articles.title: Linking tasks to OKRs
articles.body: Inside any task, use the "Linked OKR" field to connect it to a Key Result. Progress is reflected in your OKR view.

articles.title: What are OKRs?
articles.body: OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) are a goal-setting framework. An Objective is an ambitious qualitative goal; Key Results are measurable outcomes that indicate you have reached it.

articles.title: Setting your first OKR
articles.body: Go to OKRs → New Objective. Write a clear, inspiring objective for the quarter. Then add 1–5 Key Results with numeric targets.

articles.title: Weekly check-ins
articles.body: Every week, open each Key Result and update the current value. Add a confidence score and a short note. Cherut tracks the trend over time.

articles.title: Changing your plan
articles.body: Go to Settings → Billing to upgrade, downgrade or cancel your plan. Changes take effect at the end of your current billing period.

articles.title: Exporting your data
articles.body: Go to Settings → Data → Export. Your habits, tasks, OKRs, journal and all other data are exported as a single JSON file.

articles.title: Deleting your account
articles.body: Go to Settings → Account → Delete account. This permanently removes all your data. It cannot be undone. Export first if you want a copy.

hero.title: Your privacy is not a footnote.
hero.lead: Plain language. No surprises. Last updated May 2026.

privacyPolicyPage.notice: This is a plain-language summary of our privacy practices. It is designed to be readable, not exhaustive. For the full legal text, contact us at privacy@cherut.app

sections.title: What we collect
items: Your email address and name when you sign up.
Usage data: which features you use and when, to improve the product.
Content you create: habits, tasks, journal entries, OKRs. Stored encrypted.
Device and browser type for debugging and performance.

sections.title: What we don't do
items: We do not sell your data — ever. Not to advertisers, not to data brokers.
We do not show you ads. There are no ad networks in Cherut.
We do not use your journal, habits or goals to train AI models.
We do not share your personal data with third parties without your consent.

sections.title: How we store it
items: Data is stored on Firebase (Google Cloud) with encryption at rest and in transit.
Backups run daily and are retained for 30 days.
We use industry-standard TLS for all data in transit.
Access to production data is restricted to core team members.

sections.title: Your rights
items: Export: you can download all your data as JSON at any time from Settings.
Delete: you can permanently delete your account and all associated data.
Correction: you can update or correct any personal information you have provided.
Portability: your exported data is in open formats, not locked in.

sections.title: Contact
items: Questions about this policy? Email us at privacy@cherut.app
We aim to respond to all privacy inquiries within 5 business days.
For urgent data deletion requests, include "URGENT" in your subject line.
